correctness.rationale: For n≥1 and a fixed positive finite categorical p, K=s−∑1{N_i=0}. Conditioning on N_i=0 replaces p by p^{(-i)}, proving exactly Cov(K,Hhat)=∑(1−p_i)^n(M_n(p)−M_n(p^{(-i)})). Fixed-positive binomial marginal Taylor expansion yields M_n(r)=H(r)−(d−1)/(2n)+(1−∑1/r_j)/(12n²)+O_r(n^-3), including d=1. For minimum mass t, H(p)−H(q)=h(t)−tH(q)>0 since h(t)/t>−log t≥log s>log(s−1). The m minimal species dominate exponentially; the next distinct mass u gives O((1−u)^n), absent for uniform p. Independent multinomial enumeration and deletion calculation matched 40 finite cases (5 profiles, n 1..8). This finite computation is not the asymptotic proof.
residual_risks: Only fixed s, strictly positive p and IID draws; no uniformity if p_min→0 with n.
The O(n^-3) is fixed-parameter; signs for arbitrary finite n are not established.

value.rationale: Shannon entropy and observed species richness are routinely reported together. Their covariance uncertainty is not determined by either marginal or by Gini–Simpson covariance. The exact finite-n identity and sharp positive rarest-taxon exponential coefficient, universal 1/n and explicit 1/n² terms characterize their joint sampling behavior near richness saturation; a natural invariant for fixed ecological communities.
residual_risks: Ecological sampling models with unobserved species or spatial dependence fall outside the theorem.
